html:
The Chimariko were one of the smallest peoples of California, living in a few villages along a short stretch of the Trinity River in the mountains of northwestern California. Their language is an isolate, sometimes placed in the proposed Hokan group.

They fished for salmon and gathered acorns, and dealt with the Hupa downstream and with New River Shasta and Wintu neighbours. The Gold Rush of the 1850s brought miners to the Trinity, and violence and disease nearly destroyed them. The language was recorded from a few last speakers in the early 1900s and is no longer spoken.
